title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #19

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a xylophone, the short bars give (1 mark)
   A. low notes
   B. the loudest sound only
   C. no sound
   D. high notes

2. What can be used as the core of an improvised macramé ball? (1 mark)
   A. A glass bottle
   B. A metal nail
   C. Crumpled paper or old cloth
   D. A large stone

3. A player who catches the ball must not (1 mark)
   A. pass it
   B. pivot on the landing foot
   C. run with it
   D. throw it to a teammate

4. In a chest pass your thumbs turn downwards (1 mark)
   A. never
   B. when you sit
   C. as you release the ball
   D. before you catch

5. In an overhead pass, the ball starts (1 mark)
   A. above the head
   B. at the ankles
   C. between the knees
   D. behind the knees

6. Which two positions are defenders that may enter the goal circle they defend? (1 mark)
   A. WD and WA
   B. GS and C
   C. GD and GK
   D. WA and C

7. What do you add to a colour to make it darker? (1 mark)
   A. White
   B. Black
   C. Yellow
   D. Water only

8. What is a palette? (1 mark)
   A. A frame
   B. A type of paper
   C. A surface for mixing paint
   D. A kind of brush

9. Red mixed with yellow makes (1 mark)
   A. purple
   B. green
   C. brown
   D. orange

10. To paint an object so it looks round, you should (1 mark)
   A. use one flat colour only
   B. leave it blank
   C. paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   D. paint it black

11. How is flour paste made? (1 mark)
   A. Mix flour and cold water to a smooth paste, then add hot water while stirring
   B. Mix flour and sand
   C. Burn flour
   D. Freeze flour

12. In ta-te taa taa (rest), how many beats are there? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Three
   C. Five
   D. Four

13. When you see a crotchet rest, you should (1 mark)
   A. shout
   B. clap twice
   C. stop the whole song
   D. keep the beat but not clap

14. How many beats does a crotchet last? (1 mark)
   A. Half
   B. Two
   C. One
   D. Four

15. A well known children's song that uses only m r d is (1 mark)
   A. The national anthem
   B. A drum solo
   C. A song with many notes
   D. Hot Cross Buns

16. How many rectangular slabs of different sizes are cut in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Five
   C. One
   D. Ten

17. What is clay? (1 mark)
   A. A metal
   B. A kind of wood
   C. A type of paper
   D. Fine sticky soil that is soft when wet and hard when dry

18. A slab of clay is (1 mark)
   A. a hollow cup
   B. a thin roll
   C. a flat piece
   D. a round ball

19. In a medium start, the rear knee is level with (1 mark)
   A. the start line
   B. the heel of the front foot
   C. the toe of the back foot
   D. the middle of the front foot

20. Why is the national flag flown at national athletics events? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the track
   B. To decorate only
   C. It shows which country the athletes represent and builds pride
   D. To block the wind

21. How long should you hold a crab balance in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Three to five counts
   B. One hour
   C. Ten minutes
   D. Half a second

22. Where should you place your hands in a crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Behind you, shoulder-width apart
   B. In front of your face
   C. On your head
   D. In your pockets

23. If you finish a gymnastics session, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Run around wildly
   B. Leave mats on the floor
   C. Put equipment away and cool down
   D. Push the mats

24. In a side roll, you should keep your legs (1 mark)
   A. bent
   B. lifted off the mat
   C. wide apart
   D. together with toes pointed

25. A sacred song is (1 mark)
   A. a song of worship
   B. a work song only
   C. a song about a football match
   D. a song with no words

26. A song that is played fast has a (1 mark)
   A. soft dynamic
   B. low pitch
   C. long title
   D. fast tempo

27. Where must you never take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. At the school gate
   B. In the playground with permission
   C. In private places such as toilets
   D. In the classroom with permission

28. The battery of a camera (1 mark)
   A. takes the photo
   B. keeps it dry
   C. gives it power
   D. cleans the lens

29. How should you hold a camera or tablet? (1 mark)
   A. Over your head
   B. By the lens
   C. With both hands
   D. By one corner

30. A photograph is also called a (1 mark)
   A. photo
   B. montage
   C. stave
   D. drum

31. How many lines are on a staff? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. Ten
   C. Four
   D. Three

32. Why do we shower before entering the pool? (1 mark)
   A. To warm the water
   B. To keep the pool clean
   C. To learn to float
   D. To get dry

33. Why is it called the mushroom float? (1 mark)
   A. It is very tall
   B. It grows
   C. The back at the surface looks like the top of a mushroom
   D. It tastes good

34. When should you swim? (1 mark)
   A. Only when a teacher or lifeguard is watching
   B. Whenever you like
   C. Alone
   D. In the dark

35. Water games help learners to (1 mark)
   A. feel comfortable in the water
   B. study more
   C. avoid the pool
   D. forget to swim

36. Where should beginners stay in the pool? (1 mark)
   A. The shallow end
   B. Wherever
   C. Under a diving board
   D. The deep end

37. The crab walk is done (1 mark)
   A. on hands and feet with the tummy facing up
   B. face down on the tummy
   C. standing tall
   D. lying still

38. How are indigenous games mostly learnt? (1 mark)
   A. By reading long books only
   B. By watching TV only
   C. By buying kits
   D. By watching and joining in

39. Which is an example of appropriate behaviour when viewing a display? (1 mark)
   A. Touching wet paint
   B. Running
   C. Laughing at others
   D. Being quiet and respectful

40. The message of an art work is (1 mark)
   A. the price
   B. the size of the frame
   C. the artist's age
   D. what the artist wants us to learn or feel

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name the three joints of a descant recorder and state where the mouthpiece is. (3 marks)

42. State the length of a crotchet and of a quaver in beats. (2 marks)

43. Name two digital devices used for taking photographs. (2 marks)

44. Name any two players' positions in netball. (2 marks)

45. List the components of a folk song that you can analyse. (4 marks)

46. Explain how to make a shade of green. (2 marks)

47. Give four hygiene measures for using a recorder. (4 marks)

48. What is a side roll? (2 marks)

49. Describe how to compose a short melody with d, r and m, and how to check that it is a good melody. (5 marks)

50. Give three reasons for flying the Kenyan flag at an athletics event. (3 marks)

51. Give four steps of a double-handed catch. (4 marks)

52. Describe how you would enter the pool and perform a glide safely. (5 marks)

53. Explain why covering more holes makes a lower note. (3 marks)

54. Explain the meaning of diction and why it matters. (3 marks)

55. Describe how partners should give feedback on each other's gymnastics. (3 marks)

56. Explain how animal games help to keep the body healthy. (4 marks)

57. What is the East African Community? (3 marks)

58. Identify the kayamba and the drum by giving the name, the community or area and the way of playing for each. (4 marks)

59. Give the French rhythm names for a crotchet and a pair of quavers. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — high notes
   Shorter bars vibrate faster and sound higher.

2. C — Crumpled paper or old cloth
   Paper or cloth makes a soft core that keeps its shape.

3. C — run with it
   Running with the ball is against the rules.

4. C — as you release the ball
   Thumbs turn down as the arms straighten and the ball leaves the hands.

5. A — above the head
   The ball is lifted above the head before it is thrown.

6. C — GD and GK
   The Goal Defence and the Goal Keeper may play in their defending circle.

7. B — Black
   Black makes a shade, a darker tone.

8. C — A surface for mixing paint
   A palette is where paints are mixed.

9. D — orange
   Red and yellow together give orange.

10. C — paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   Tones make an object look solid and round.

11. A — Mix flour and cold water to a smooth paste, then add hot water while stirring
   An adult adds hot water to thicken the smooth paste.

12. D — Four
   Each of ta-te, taa, taa and the rest fills one beat, so there are four beats.

13. D — keep the beat but not clap
   A rest is a silent beat, and the beat continues.

14. C — One
   A crotchet lasts for one beat.

15. D — Hot Cross Buns
   Hot Cross Buns uses only three notes.

16. A — Three
   Three slabs are cut, one for each of d, r and m.

17. D — Fine sticky soil that is soft when wet and hard when dry
   Clay is a fine, sticky soil used for modelling.

18. C — a flat piece
   A slab is a flat sheet of clay.

19. D — the middle of the front foot
   The medium start places the rear knee by the middle of the front foot.

20. C — It shows which country the athletes represent and builds pride
   The flag is a symbol of the country.

21. A — Three to five counts
   Hold the balance for three to five slow counts.

22. A — Behind you, shoulder-width apart
   Hands go behind you, about shoulder-width apart.

23. C — Put equipment away and cool down
   Tidying and cooling down are good habits.

24. D — together with toes pointed
   Legs stay together to keep the log shape.

25. A — a song of worship
   Sacred songs praise God, give thanks or teach faith.

26. D — fast tempo
   Tempo is speed.

27. C — In private places such as toilets
   Privacy must be respected.

28. C — gives it power
   Without power the device will not work.

29. C — With both hands
   Two hands prevent dropping.

30. A — photo
   Photo is short for photograph.

31. A — Five
   The staff has five lines.

32. B — To keep the pool clean
   It removes dirt and sweat.

33. C — The back at the surface looks like the top of a mushroom
   The rounded back at the top looks like a mushroom cap.

34. A — Only when a teacher or lifeguard is watching
   Supervision keeps swimmers safe.

35. A — feel comfortable in the water
   They build confidence.

36. A — The shallow end
   Shallow water is safer.

37. A — on hands and feet with the tummy facing up
   It is like the crab balance, but moving.

38. D — By watching and joining in
   Elders and children play together.

39. D — Being quiet and respectful
   Respect for others' work is important.

40. D — what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   The message is the idea communicated.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Head joint, middle joint and foot joint. The mouthpiece is on the head joint.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the joints, 1 mark for order or naming all, 1 mark for the mouthpiece.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A crotchet is one beat and a quaver is half a beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smartphone, tablet, digital camera. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Goal Shooter, Goal Attack, Wing Attack, Centre, Wing Defence, Goal Defence, Goal Keeper. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Community of origin, type or occasion, message, participants and their roles, and instruments.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct components.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Add a small amount of black to green, and more if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for black, 1 mark for adding a little.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands before playing; do not share it without cleaning; do not eat while playing; wipe the mouthpiece; clean it properly. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: A roll along the mat sideways with the body straight and long like a log.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sideways roll, 1 mark for the straight body.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give each note a syllable, using steps. End on d. Sing it with hand signs. Check that it has variation and stepwise motion and that it ends on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five valid points.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: It shows which country the athletes represent; it builds pride and patriotism; it brings people together to cheer; it shows respect to visitors. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Watch the ball into your hands; reach out with both hands; spread the fingers with the thumbs close; bend the arms and pull the ball to the chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Get permission and warm up. Enter feet first by the steps or sit and slide. Stay in shallow water. Stand with the back to the wall and stretch the arms overhead. Put feet on the wall, breathe, put the face in, push off gently and glide with a straight body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five parts.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: The column of air inside becomes longer, and a longer air column vibrates more slowly, giving a lower note.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for longer air column, 2 marks for lower note.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Diction is saying the words clearly. It matters because the audience can understand the message of the song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watch carefully, say one good thing first, then one thing to improve, and be kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: They strengthen muscles, stretch the body, improve balance and coordination and make the heart and lungs stronger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: A group of countries in East Africa that work together on matters such as trade, travel and peace.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of countries, 1 mark for East Africa, 1 mark for working together.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Kayamba: coastal people such as the Mijikenda, played by shaking. Drum (ngoma): found in many communities, played with hands or sticks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name, community or area and method, up to 4.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Crotchet: taa. Pair of quavers: ta-te.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
